steps.title: Open the Desk
steps.narration: This is the Desk, a daily briefing. It lists the symbols sitting closest to a real support or resistance wall, plus a history of every past briefing.
steps.point_out: Four panels: Provenance, Briefing, Skipped Members, and Screen History.

steps.title: Look back at a past day's briefing
steps.narration: Click any date in the history list and the page instantly shows exactly what was recorded that day. Nothing is recalculated — it is a plain read-back of the saved snapshot.
steps.point_out: A banner confirms you are now viewing 2026-06-22, not today's screen.

expect.text: Viewing the recorded screen for 2026-06-22 — not the latest.

steps.title: Snap back to today with one click
steps.narration: A "Latest" button shows up whenever you are looking at an older day. Click it and the page returns to today's screen right away, with no waiting.
steps.point_out: The banner disappears and today's briefing is back on screen.

steps.title: Select that past day again
steps.narration: Selecting 2026-06-22 once more sets up the next step: jumping from one of its rows straight into a deeper chart.

expect.text: Viewing the recorded screen for 2026-06-22 — not the latest.

steps.title: Jump from a briefing row straight into its chart
steps.narration: Click any symbol in the Briefing list and it opens the deeper chart page already filled in and already loaded. There is no retyping the symbol or the date.
steps.point_out: The chart page opens with AAPL's real wall already drawn, at the band 298.02–300.1001.

steps.title: Back to the Desk
steps.narration: Returning to the Desk to show the other kind of row: one that was skipped because it had no recorded price history.
steps.point_out: The Desk is back to its normal view.

steps.title: Select the same past day once more
steps.narration: Selecting 2026-06-22 again brings back the list of symbols that were skipped that day.
steps.point_out: The 91 skipped symbols are listed again, including ABBV.

expect.text: Viewing the recorded screen for 2026-06-22 — not the latest.

steps.title: A skipped symbol still opens honestly
steps.narration: Skipped symbols are clickable too. Clicking one still opens the deeper chart page, but it tells the truth: no price history was recorded for it, instead of showing a made-up chart.
steps.point_out: "No bar series recorded for ABBV." appears instead of a fabricated chart.

expect.text: No bar series recorded for ABBV.

steps.title: Opening the chart page on its own still works the old way
steps.narration: Opened directly, with no symbol or date already picked, the chart page looks exactly as it always has. Both fields stay empty until you choose a symbol and press Load.
steps.point_out: Both fields are empty and the page waits for you, unchanged from before this update.

expect.text: Choose a symbol and an as-of time, then Load, to see its tradable level map.

steps.title: The old manual way still works too
steps.narration: Typing a symbol by hand still works exactly as before. This update only added new shortcuts — it did not change the original way of using the page.
steps.point_out: "AAPL" is now typed into the Symbol field.

steps.title: Fill in today's date with one click
steps.narration: A "Today" button fills in the as-of date for you, saving a manual date entry.
steps.point_out: The as-of field now shows today's date.

steps.title: Load the chart by hand
steps.narration: Pressing Load fills in the tradable-level table exactly as it always has, proving the original manual workflow is untouched by this update.
steps.point_out: The bands table appears, same as always.
